items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions the Ertegun brothers as staunch supporters of jazz, but the interviewee (Teddy Wilson) does not respond to this specific mention or provide any personal anecdote or connection regarding them.

ctx.x: But those people used jazz, and those are the parasites, and that's a cynical way to break into the field, by criticizing a big name singer and saying she stinks. But that is cynical, like the Ayatollah, he doesn't care whose head rolls, or like Hitler did, that kind of mentality. So many in the jazz world are not sincere, associated with the jazz movement. They don't respect jazz musicians. A lot of these guys come around simpering and smiling, with their little pencils and papers, people with the magazines, and…

Like Atlantic Records, the Ertegun brothers, they were staunch supporters, their father was the Ambassador to Turkey years ago, and once they got a taste of American Ambassador from Turkey to the U.S.
* Frazier did frequently write about jazz throughout his life. -CJ.
